title: Weekly price shock alert: BCI cotton - week ended July 24
content:
BCI cotton prices split across Asia in the week ended July 24, with Pakistan's KCA spot rate up 1.07 per cent, China's 3128B up 0.62 per cent and India's Shankar-6 flat.
The divergence changes raw-cotton cost visibility for mills, yarn exporters and apparel sourcing teams.
Indian yarn may offer steadier quotes; Pakistan and China need closer checks on cotton buying and yarn pass-through.

title: Bangladesh begins 800-acre China-backed industrial zone in Chattogram
content:
Bangladesh has begun the 800-acre Chattogram Chinese economic zone to expand export manufacturing and draw about $500 million in foreign investment.
Local fabric and accessory production by Chinese firms could help garment makers cut lead times, logistics and production costs.
Authorities expect 60 per cent of plots to be factory-ready within three years; the project is due by December 31, 2031.

title: China's industrial firms' H1 profits rise 18.7%
content:
China’s industrial firms above designated size posted an 18.7 per cent YoY profit increase in H1 2026. 
Combined profits reached 3.95 trillion yuan in January-June, covering firms with annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan. 
The data offers textile, apparel and sourcing teams a current gauge of China’s large industrial sector.

title: Polyester prices rise sharply in India amid Hormuz oil risks
content:
India’s polyester chain strengthened as Strait of Hormuz tensions lifted crude oil and petrochemical feedstock costs.
PTA, PSF and polyester yarn prices rose, while China’s PTA and MEG remained volatile.
Indian buyers stayed cautious and purchased largely on a need basis, as uncertainty persisted over the sustainability of recent price hikes.

title: Can Madhya Pradesh become India’s next textile growth engine?
content:
Madhya Pradesh’s Indore-Dhar belt is emerging as a textile hub around the 2,156-acre PM MITRA Park at Bhainsola near Badnawar.
The project has reported commitments exceeding ₹20,000 crore and is projected to create more than 46,000 jobs.
Plug-and-play facilities, highway links and investor interest could support exporters, apparel makers and sourcing teams.

title: FICCI flags 9 challenges limiting Bangladesh’s investment potential
content:
The Foreign Investors’ Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Bangladesh has identified nine interlinked challenges, including regulatory uncertainty, high logistics costs and financial sector fragility, that are limiting investment potential. 
It also flagged infrastructure gaps, poor global competitiveness, fragmented institutions, skills shortages, a complex tax regime and transparency concerns.

title: US’ 10% duty under Section 301; India looking quota for T&A under BTA
content:
India is seeking US textile market-access benefits comparable to Bangladesh and Cambodia under a proposed TRQ mechanism.
Inclusion could offer zero-duty access within specified quotas, helping Indian exporters offset the additional 10 per cent tariff.
The issue is part of ongoing India-US BTA talks, while the US quota mechanism is yet to be operationalised.

title: Norway apparel imports grow; India's market share slips in Jan-April
content:
Norway's apparel imports rose 5 per cent to $806.86 million in January-April 2026, but India's exports slipped to $36.32 million, reducing its market share to 4.50 per cent.
While China, Bangladesh and Vietnam expanded shipments, India struggled to capitalise on cotton apparel demand.
Strengthening MMF capabilities and value-added products could improve its position.
